mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-28.7 to -39.4) with accelerating weekly losses. This momentum reflects entrenched suppression of discretionary outings that persists absent any countervailing signal, so the trend continues downward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean despite three or more prior consecutive weekly declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week PARKS drop of more than 10 points (from -7.6 to -19.9) signals newly tightened outdoor-activity enforcement under the extended state of emergency, which spills over to suppress retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -7.6 to -19.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks despite the PARKS threshold being crossed in the current week.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous steep declines in TRANSIT (-40.7) and WORKPLACES (-39.7) indicate compounded reduction in both commuting and errand-linked trips; their joint collapse amplifies the drop in retail footfall beyond what either series alone would predict, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fell over 10 points in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next two weeks is no larger than predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone, or RETAIL_REC rebounds despite continued joint decline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen every week for four consecutive weeks (1.9 to 3.0), indicating a behavioral shift toward staying home that is characteristic of entrenched emergency-period routines; this sustained rise predicts continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as long as the state of emergency remains active.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased monotonically from 1.9 to 3.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL continues to rise, indicating decoupling of stay-home behavior from retail suppression.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-August coincides with the Japanese Obon holiday period, during which retail and recreation mobility typically dips further due to travel and family visits rather than policy effects, then partially rebounds within one week after the holiday window closes, producing a short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: current week falls within or immediately after the Obon holiday period (mid-August)
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-08-15 falls within the typical Obon holiday window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rebound within one week after the Obon period despite the seasonal trigger being active, and instead continues declining.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week decline in RETAIL_REC has accelerated from -1.1 to -5.8 to -6.0 points, suggesting intensifying enforcement of the extended state of emergency; once the weekly decline magnitude exceeds 5 points, enforcement effects compound and predict further acceleration of the decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week RETAIL_REC decline exceeds 5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:weekly RETAIL_REC declines widened from -1.1 to -5.8 to -6.0 points
failure_condition: The pace of RETAIL_REC decline slows or reverses within two weeks despite two consecutive weeks of greater than 5-point drops.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined far less steeply than RETAIL_REC (-18.1 vs -39.4), showing that essential trips are preserved while discretionary retail is selectively suppressed; this persistent gap between essential and discretionary mobility categories predicts continued relative weakness in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell to -18.1 while RETAIL_REC fell to -39.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows substantially while RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks, contradicting the selective-suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling TRANSIT (down 10.6 points over three weeks) and rising RESIDENTIAL (up 1.1 points over the same period) jointly indicates a structural shift toward home-centered routines that reduces trip-chaining to retail destinations, compounding to drive RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks beyond either signal's individual effect.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -30.1 to -40.7 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 1.9 to 3.0 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds over the next four weeks even as TRANSIT continues falling and RESIDENTIAL continues rising, indicating no compounding interaction effect.
